dataset_status.reason: The runtime has no installed Parquet engine (pyarrow/fastparquet). No validation score is fabricated.

outcome_stat.definition: Outcome percentage = positive outcome rate; bootstrap 95% CI uses row-level resampling; change_vs_baseline = synthetic outcome rate minus real/baseline outcome rate.

fidelity_checks.correlation: Pearson correlation matrix comparison using Frobenius norm and mean absolute correlation difference
fidelity_checks.train_on_synthetic_test_on_real: Classifier trained only on synthetic rows and evaluated on held-out real rows; ROC-AUC, accuracy, F1
fidelity_checks.real_vs_synthetic_classifier: Classifier attempts to distinguish real from synthetic; ROC-AUC near 0.5 is desirable
fidelity_checks.subgroup_fidelity: Per subgroup with n >= 30; smaller subgroups are retained but flagged with warning
fidelity_checks.distance_to_closest_real_record: Nearest-neighbor distance after robust scaling; reports mean/median/p95 and exact/near-duplicate rate

viva_evidence: A strong synthetic dataset should preserve marginal distributions, pairwise relationships, subgroup behavior and downstream utility without making real-vs-synthetic classification easy.
For TSTR, a useful synthetic dataset should support a model that generalizes to real held-out data.
For the real-vs-synthetic classifier, ROC-AUC close to 0.5 indicates weak distinguishability; substantially above 0.5 indicates detectable synthetic artifacts.
Subgroup checks are only treated as statistically stable when n >= 30; smaller groups receive an explicit warning.
Nearest-real-record distance is a privacy/fidelity diagnostic: unusually small distances can indicate memorization or duplication.
